Born to a Tutsi family that fled to Uganda when he was two, this politician commanded a rebel force that ended the 1994 genocide in his home country and has served as its president since 2000 — who is he?
Paul Kagame: President of Rwanda since 2000. The RPF was one of the main belligerents of the Rwandan Civil War and was the armed force which ended the 1994 Rwandan genocide.
The first Kerala Chief Minister to win re-election after completing a full term, this CPI(M) leader represented the Dharmadom constituency — who is he?
Which Chinese diplomat rocketed to foreign minister in December 2022, then vanished from public view six months later and was quietly removed by July 2023?
Also known as Calvinism, this 16th-century Protestant branch stresses biblical authority, God's sovereignty, and covenant theology as articulated by John Calvin — what movement is this?
Nicknamed 'Captain Comeback,' this Naval Academy grad won the 1963 Heisman Trophy, served a tour in Vietnam, then led the Dallas Cowboys to two Super Bowl titles — who is he?
Roger Staubach: American football player and Navy officer (born 1942)

As students in 1930s Paris, this Syrian and Michel Aflaq cooked up a doctrine blending nationalism and socialism, then co-founded the Ba'ath Party — and decades later he was assassinated in Paris. Who is it?
Sparked when Qing officials seized a British-registered ship called the Arrow in 1856, this conflict between Britain, France, and China forced the legalization of the drug trade — which conflict?
Second Opium War: 1856–1860 war between British–French forces and China.
In 1968 she became the first Black woman elected to the U.S. Congress, and in 1972 the first Black major-party presidential candidate — who was she?
Formed after the October Revolution of 1917 and dissolved in 1991, this Moscow-based superpower was the largest country on Earth by area — which one?
Soviet Union: Country in Eurasia from 1922 to 1991.
Born to a Cossack family in Poltava, this journalist-turned-revolutionary became Supreme Commander of the Ukrainian People's Army during the Ukrainian War of Independence — who was he?
Serving as Dachau's second commandant and later the first inspector of Nazi concentration camps, this SS commander was killed in 1943 when his plane was shot down over Kharkov — who was he?
Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich of Russia
This Japanese term describes marginalized, often homeless youth — a mix of runaways and those seeking community after bullying — who gather in Kabukicho's back alleys. What is this subculture called?
Toyoko kids: Youth group in Tokyo, Japan.
Composed in an archaic Sanskrit dialect, this collection of four ancient hymn texts forms the oldest layer of Hindu scripture — what are they collectively called?
This Warring States-era Chinese general commanded conquests of three rival kingdoms and is remembered by tradition as one of the four greatest generals of the late Warring States period — who was he?
Wang Jian (Qin): 3rd century BC Chinese military general.
Famous for pioneering sensationalist 'yellow journalism,' this publisher fought a fierce circulation war against Joseph Pulitzer's New York paper after acquiring a rival New York daily — who was he?
William Randolph Hearst: American newspaper publisher (1863–1951)
A former Palmach commando, this Israeli general became the first prime minister born in the region of Palestine — and was assassinated while serving a second term in 1995. Who was he?
Yitzhak Rabin: Prime Minister of Israel (1974–1977; 1992–1995)
A dispute between two rival lords escalated into a decade-long Japanese civil war from 1467 to 1477 that triggered the Warring States period — what was this conflict called?
Ōnin War: 15th-century civil war in Japan.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Qian Xuesen (born 1911) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared first?
Lisp (programming language) (published 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Mark Oliphant is a physicist. Born and raised in Adelaide, South Australia, Oliphant graduated from the University of Adelaide in 1922.
Who among these is a chemist?
Carolyn Bertozzi is a chemist. Carolyn Ruth Bertozzi (born October 10, 1966) is an American chemist and Nobel laureate, known for her wide-ranging work spanning both chemistry and biology.
What is the atomic number of Fluorine?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
In what year was Bernie Madoff born?
Bernie Madoff: Madoff's firm had two basic units: a stock brokerage and an asset management business; the Ponzi scheme was centered in the asset management business.
In what year was H. H. Holmes born?
H. H. Holmes: Holmes, was an American con artist and serial killer active between 1891 and 1894.
In what year was Alan Turing born?
Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year did Émile Durkheim die?
Émile Durkheim: David Émile Durkheim (French: [emil dyʁkɛm] or [dyʁkajm]; 15 April 1858 – 15 November 1917) was a French sociologist.
In what year did Ferdinand Porsche die?
Ferdinand Porsche (3 September 1875 – 30 January 1951) was an Austrian-German automotive engineer and founder of the Porsche AG.
In what year was Citric acid discovered?
Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
In what year was Gold discovered?
Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
Methylprednisolone: Pfizer. It is either used at low doses for chronic illnesses or used at high doses during acute flares.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet family based?
Embraer E-Jet family: Brazil. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Tantalum?
Tantalum: Anders Gustaf Ekeberg. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
Who is credited with discovering L'Hôpital's rule?
L'Hôpital's rule: Johann Bernoulli. The differentiation of the numerator and denominator often simplifies the quotient or converts it to a limit that can be directly evaluated by continuity.
Who is credited with discovering Sulfur?
Sulfur: Antoine Lavoisier. Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
Formed by the angle of thyroid cartilage around the voice box, this neck protrusion becomes a prominent secondary sex characteristic in most men during puberty — what is it commonly called?
Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.
Ranging from South Florida to Peru, this reptile is the most widespread member of its family in the Americas and one of only two species that commonly thrive in saltwater — which species?
American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) is a species of crocodilian found in the Neotropics.
A physician who called medicine his lawful wife and literature his mistress, this Russian writer produced four stage classics and ranks among modernism's founders — who is he?
Anton Chekhov was Russian dramatist and author (1860–1904).
Caused by poor circulation, lost nerve supply, or simple disuse, this process shrinks a cell, organ, or tissue below its normal mature size — what's it called?
Atrophy is the partial or complete wasting away of a part of the body.
Native to Southeast Asia, the glossy heart-shaped leaves of this evergreen vine are chewed together with areca nut — name the plant?
Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
First described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado, this sauropod dinosaur's Greek name means arm lizard, a reference to its proportionately long front limbs — what genus is it?
Brachiosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
The leaves and buds of this evergreen shrub, when processed differently, yield green, black, oolong, white, and yellow varieties of the world's most popular hot beverage — what's the species?
Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
Taken by mouth with effects lasting about a day, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever, hives, and dermatitis with less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what is it?
Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
Marked by a stopped heartbeat and halted breathing, this reversible-sounding medical state was given its name once CPR and defibrillation made post-arrest resuscitation possible — what's it called?
Clinical death is the medical term for cessation of blood circulation and breathing, the two criteria necessary to sustain the lives of human beings and of many other organisms.
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.

Native to Madagascar and grown as an ornamental tree throughout the tropics, this legume species has fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red flowers; its wild origin wasn't confirmed until 1932. What tree is this?
Delonix regia is a species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae, subfamily Caesalpinioideae native to Madagascar.

Massive enough to be rounded by its own gravity but too small to clear its orbital neighborhood like the solar system's eight major planets, Pluto became the prototype of this category after a 2006 reclassification. Name the category?

Dwarf planet is a small planetary-mass object that is in direct orbit around the Sun, massive enough to be gravitationally rounded, but insufficient to achieve orbital dominance like the eight classical planets of the Solar System.

Often used to keep blood pressure from dropping during anesthesia, this stimulant has also been tried against asthma, obesity, and even narcolepsy — though it's no longer the preferred fix. What is it?
Ephedrine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and sympathomimetic agent that is often used to prevent low blood pressure during anesthesia.
A Swiss linguist and philosopher who died in 1913, this thinker's ideas shaped 20th-century linguistics, psychoanalysis, and anthropology alike, according to one of his translators — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure (26 November 1857 - 22 February 1913) was a Swiss linguist, semiotician and philosopher.
Its name comes from Greek for 'milk flower,' and this small genus of about 20 bulbous perennials nods with a single white bell of six tepals — what is the botanical name for the snowdrop?
Galanthus (from Ancient Greek, (gla, "milk") + (nthos, "flower")), or snowdrop, is a small genus of approximately 20 species of bulbous perennial herbaceous plants in the family Amaryllidaceae.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
Tapeworms, flukes, and roundworms burrowing into the gut and beyond all fall under this macroparasitic disease — a neglected tropical illness better known as worm infection. What is it?
Helminthiasis is any macroparasitic disease of humans and other animals in which a part of the body is infected with parasitic worms, known as helminths.

Also called prussic acid, this highly toxic and flammable liquid boils just above room temperature at 25.6 degrees Celsius. It is produced industrially as a precursor to many chemical compounds, particularly potassium cyanide and adiponitrile. What is it?
Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula HCN.
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'violet,' fitting for an element that boils into a violet gas — and it sits at atomic number 53 as the heaviest stable halogen. What is it?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
The youngest division chief in GM history, this engineer shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the company behind a famously gull-winged car — who was he?
John DeLorean (d-; January 6, 1925 - March 19, 2005) was an American engineer, inventor, and executive in the U.S.
Despite its name suggesting a root vegetable, this biennial cultivar of wild cabbage grows a swollen edible stem above ground and is related to broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts — what is it?
Kohlrabi (scientific name Brassica oleracea Gongylodes Group), also called German turnip or turnip cabbage, is a biennial vegetable, a low, stout cultivar of wild cabbage.
At the time of her death, this French heiress and cosmetics-empire shareholder was the richest woman in the world, worth over $44 billion. Who is she?
Liliane Bettencourt (ne Schueller; 21 October 1922 - 21 September 2017) was a French heiress, socialite and businesswoman.
Which group of vividly colored, long-tailed New World parrots — prized in aviculture though some species face conservation concerns — belongs to the tribe Arini?
Macaw are a group of large New World parrots that are long-tailed and often colorful, in the tribe Arini.
This small southern-African mongoose has digging foreclaws and a knack for thermoregulating in harsh, dry country, living in tight packs of up to 30 — which sharp-eyed animal is it?
Meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
By dividing one cell into two with an identical set of chromosomes apiece, this stage of the cell cycle keeps genetic stability intact across generations — what is it?
Mitosis is a part of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.
A white crystalline solid built from two fused benzene rings, this aromatic compound is the main ingredient of traditional mothballs and has an odor you can smell at just 0.08 ppm. What is it?
Naphthalene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C10H8.
Also called the coypu, this plant-eating rodent digs streamside burrows and now troubles several countries as an invasive species far from its South American home — what is it?
Nutria (Myocastor coypus) is an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent from South America.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
Fill in the blank: “____ (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.”

Peter Madsen (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur. Peter Langkjær Madsen (Danish: [ˈpʰe̝ˀtɐ ˈlɑŋˌkʰeˀɐ̯ ˈmæsn̩]; born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.

One of 36 species-rich pit vipers found mainly in the Americas, this snake shakes a noisy tail segment to warn off predators and is responsible for most snakebite injuries in North America — which snake?
Rattlesnake are venomous snakes that form the genera Crotalus and Sistrurus of the subfamily Crotalinae (the pit vipers).
The first alkali metal denser than water, this element has a radioactive isotope with a half-life more than three times the age of the universe — which element?
Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
Which chemical element, symbol Se, was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius and named for the moon, in a nod to its chemical similarity to tellurium, named for the Earth?
Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
With the formula CH3COONa, this colorless, moisture-absorbing salt of acetic acid is deliquescent, meaning it can even dissolve in the water it pulls from the air — which compound?
Sodium acetate is a chemical compound with formula CH3COONa, also abbreviated NaOAc.

This medical emergency occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or reduced, causing cell death — its warning signs include facial drooping and sudden difficulty speaking or moving one side of the body. Name the condition?

Stroke is a medical condition in which blood flow to a part of the brain is reduced or blocked causing cell death. There are two main types of stroke: ischemic, due to lack of blood flow, and hemorrhagic, due to bleeding.
This fibrous connective tissue connects muscle to bone, unlike its cousin which connects bone to bone, and numbers about 4,000 throughout the adult human body — what is it?
Tendon is a tough band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects muscle to bone.

This field of geoscience studies the forms and features of land surfaces — not just elevation and relief, but also roads, boundaries, and buildings as recorded on detailed maps — what's this field called?
Topography is the study of forms and features of land surfaces. The topography of an area may refer to landforms and features themselves, or a description or depiction in maps.
As head of the WWII Office of Scientific Research and Development, this MIT engineer steered nearly all American military R&D, including radar and the early Manhattan Project — who was he?
Vannevar Bush (van-; March 11, 1890 - June 28, 1974) was an American engineer, inventor and science administrator, who during World War II headed the U.S.
This Austrian physicist earned a 1945 Nobel Prize for the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the existence of what would become known as the neutrino — who is he?
Wolfgang Pauli (25 April 1900 - 15 December 1958) was an Austrian theoretical physicist and a pioneer of quantum mechanics.
This bird-of-prey family boasts 256 species including eagles, hawks, kites, and harriers, though the osprey and secretary bird are classified separately — which family is it?
Accipitridae: Family of birds of prey. The Accipitridae have a cosmopolitan distribution, being found on all the world's continents (except Antarctica) and a number of oceanic island groups.
Conceived as a clean-sheet 'extra wide body' answer to Boeing's Dreamliner, this twin-engine jet first lifted off from Toulouse in 2013 on Rolls-Royce Trent power — which airliner is it?
Airbus A350: Large twin-aisle airliner family.
Refined from bauxite and nicknamed alumina, this compound shows up in nature as the mineral corundum — the very stuff of rubies and sapphires. What is it?
Aluminium oxide: Chemical compound. Aluminium oxide (or aluminium(III) oxide) is a chemical compound of aluminium and oxygen with the chemical formula Al2O3.
Named for a 19th-century Swedish physicist and symbolized by a letter of the Swedish alphabet, which unit of length equals one ten-billionth of a metre, handy for measuring atoms and bond lengths?
Angstrom: Unit of length. The unit is named after the Swedish physicist Anders Jonas Ångström (1814–1874).

Studying humanity's past through the recovery of artifacts and sites — including stone tools dating back 3.3 million years — this discipline sits at the crossroads of the social sciences and humanities — which field?
Archaeology: Study of human activity based on materials left behind.
Affecting roughly one in five people at some point and usually starting in childhood, this long-term itchy, red, cracked-skin condition is also simply called eczema — what's its formal name?
Atopic dermatitis: Long-term form of skin inflammation.
Named for the physicist who shared a 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie, this SI unit measures one radioactive decay event per second — which unit?
Becquerel: SI derived unit of radioactivity.
This class of aquatic molluscs — including clams, oysters, mussels, and scallops — has no head and encloses its soft body in a hinged pair of shells called valves — which class?
Bivalvia: Class of molluscs. The shell of a bivalve is composed of calcium carbonate, and consists of two, usually similar, parts called valves.
Named in honor of physicist Satyendra Nath Bose and coined by Paul Dirac, this class of subatomic particle has integer spin and includes force carriers like gluons and the Higgs — what is it called?
Boson: Class of subatomic particle. In particle physics, a boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
Belonging to the superfamily Papilionoidea, these brightly winged insects pass through a chrysalis stage, and their oldest fossils date to about 56 million years ago — what are they?
Butterfly: Group of insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also known as meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the Apiaceae family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — what is it?
Caraway: Species of plant in the carrot family.

Also known as gotu kola or Indian pennywort, this herbaceous perennial from the Apiaceae family is eaten as a vegetable and used in traditional medicine across Africa, Asia, and the Pacific — what is it?
Centella asiatica: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.
Packed with chlorophyll, this plant-cell organelle captures sunlight, splits water to release oxygen, and feeds sugar-making in the Calvin cycle — what is it called?
Chloroplast: Plant organelle that conducts photosynthesis.

Medieval German miners cursed an ore that looked metal-rich but smelted into nothing useful, naming it after a mischievous goblin — yet for centuries its blue pigment tinted glass and jewelry. Which element, symbol Co, atomic number 27, earned that goblin's name?
Cobalt: Chemical element with atomic number 27 (Co)
Considered the most renowned Greek mathematician since antiquity, he advanced measure theory and the calculus of variations and even gave thermodynamics an axiomatic formulation — who is it?
Native to the Andes and Mesoamerica, this plant genus includes five edible species known variously as squash, pumpkin or gourd — which genus?
Native to Madagascar and grown ornamentally throughout the tropics, this legume tree is known for its fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red blossoms — what is it?
Delonix regia: Species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae.
Also nicknamed the French Mastiff, this large, powerfully muscled brachycephalic breed ranks among France's heaviest dogs — which breed?
Dogue de Bordeaux: Dog breed originating in France.

A British physicist who hauled a captured German thermionic valve back from the Western Front, he won the 1947 Nobel for mapping the ionosphere — work that paved the way for radar and shortwave radio. Who was he?

Native across the arctic and temperate Northern Hemisphere, this fern relative grows both a spore-bearing stem and a separate sterile green one, and is often mistaken for mare's tail — what plant is it?
The only member of its family found outside the Americas, this tiny insect-eating bird holds its short tail erect and is unusually polygynous for a songbird — what is it?
Eurasian wren: Species of bird. In Anglophone Europe, it is commonly known simply as the wren.
Marketed under brand names like Allegra, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergy symptoms without crossing the blood-brain barrier the way older drugs do — what medication is it?
Fexofenadine: Antihistamine medication. Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.

A particle physicist who later turned cattle rancher and founded San Francisco's Exploratorium, he was blacklisted by McCarthyism partly for being a more famous physicist's younger brother — who was he?
Frank Oppenheimer: American particle physicist and science educator (1912–1985)
Pioneered by Gregor Mendel's 19th-century pea plant experiments in Brno, this branch of biology studies heredity and trait inheritance — what is it?
Genetics: Science of genes, heredity and variation.

Identified in 1898 by an Italian pathologist and later named in his honor, this cell organelle packages proteins into vesicles and adds sugar chains before shipping them to their destination. What is it called?
Golgi apparatus: Cell organelle that packages proteins for export.
A lentivirus and member of the retrovirus family, it gradually cripples the human immune system — and untreated, leaves roughly 9 to 11 years before the immune collapse called AIDS. What is it?
HIV: Human retrovirus, cause of AIDS. Without treatment, the average survival time after infection with HIV is estimated to be 9 to 11 years, depending on the HIV subtype.

This 19th-century American economist argued in his bestseller 'Progress and Poverty' that a single tax on land values could build a fairer, more productive society — sparking a movement named for him. Who was he?
An American aviator and aerospace engineer who first made his name as a big-budget Hollywood producer, this man grew famous late in life for his reclusive, eccentric ways — who was the magnate?
Howard Hughes: American aviator, aerospace engineer and business magnate (1905–1976)
This family of long-legged wading birds that live in wetlands and forests lent its name — mistakenly — to the scientific name of the western cattle egret in 1757 — what's the bird group called?
Ibis: Long-legged wading birds with down-curved beaks.
Sold under the brand name Accutane, this vitamin A-related retinoid treats severe cystic acne but commonly causes dry lips, dry skin, and increased sunburn risk — what is it called?
Isotretinoin: Medication primarily used to treat severe acne.
This German craftsman's mechanical printing press — with its oil-based ink and adjustable metal type — sparked an information revolution that helped fuel the Renaissance and Reformation — who is he?
Johannes Gutenberg: German inventor and craftsman (c. 1393–1406 – 1468)
This Canadian atmospheric scientist holds a chair in public policy at Texas Tech and in 2021 became chief scientist of the Nature Conservancy — who is she?
Katharine Hayhoe: Canadian atmospheric scientist. Katharine Anne Scott Hayhoe (born 1972) is a Canadian atmospheric scientist.
Commonly called the voice box, which organ in the upper neck houses the vocal cords and protects the windpipe from food entering it?
Larynx: Voice box, an organ in the neck of amphibians, reptiles, and mammals.
The only person ever to win two unshared Nobel Prizes, this American chemist earned one for his work on the chemical bond and another for peace activism — who is he?
Linus Pauling: American scientist and activist (1901–1994)
This American experimental physicist won the 1968 Nobel Prize for discovering resonance states using the hydrogen bubble chamber — who was he?
Luis Walter Alvarez: American physicist, inventor and professor (1911–1988)

Often called the mirror image of depression, this psychiatric state brings racing thoughts, pressured speech, boundless energy, and a shrinking need for sleep — what is this elevated mood syndrome called?
Mania: State of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
Isolated in 1958 from cow pineal glands because it could lighten frog skin, this nighttime brain hormone turned out to be the body's regulator of the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin: Hormone released by the pineal gland.
Succeeding the Castro brothers, this engineer became Cuba's first head of state in nearly six decades who wasn't a member of that family — who is he?
Miguel Díaz-Canel: Leader of Cuba since 2021.
Named for its rough alignment with the Moon's cycle — the two words are even linguistic cognates — this calendar unit varies from 28 to 31 days in the Gregorian system — what is it?
Month: Unit of time, usually 28 to 31 days.
The only mammal that's essentially cold-blooded, this burrowing "sand puppy" of the Horn of Africa also lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen — what creature is it?
This reddish-brown, poisonous gas (formula NO2) is a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer — and your gas stove quietly produces it while you cook. What is it?
Named after the Greek word for tumor, first used this way by the physician Galen nearly two millennia ago, this medical field focuses on diagnosing and treating cancer — what is it called?
Oncology: Branch of medicine dealing with, or specializing in, cancer.
This condition inflames a large organ behind the stomach, sending severe upper-abdominal pain into the back, with chronic cases bringing weight loss and fatty stool — what is it?
A famous singer known for her CCTV New Year's Gala appearances, she has served as China's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?
Peng Liyuan: First Lady of China since 2012. Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).
With a phosphate-charged head and two fatty-acid tails joined by glycerol, this molecule builds neuron membranes and can decline up to 20% by age 80 — what is it?

Its methods range from gentle negotiation and lawmaking all the way to warfare against adversaries, and the social science that studies it tacks 'science' onto its name; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics: Activities associated with group decisions.

Built from long chains of amino acid residues, these biomolecules fold into specific 3D shapes that catalyze reactions, copy DNA, and ferry molecules around the cell. What are these workhorse macromolecules?
Protein: Biomolecule consisting of chains of amino acid residues.
The sole member of its genus and a relative of apples and pears, this hard, aromatic golden fruit is too tart to enjoy raw but turns lovely as jam or a fragrant cheese — what is it?
With the widest geographic range of any non-human primate, this brown-to-grey Old World monkey lives in matrilineal troops of up to 200 individuals — which species?
Rhesus macaque: Species of Old World monkey. The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.
What term describes herbivorous mammals like cattle and giraffes that digest plant matter by regurgitating and re-chewing it as cud?
Ruminant: Hoofed herbivorous grazing or browsing mammals.
About 90% of cases trace to a herniated spinal disc pressing on a nerve root, producing a shooting pain that runs from the lower back down one leg — what's the condition?
Sciatica: Lower-back pain that can extend down the leg.
Nicknamed the 'brushwood dog' for its game-flushing hunting style, this is the smallest of Japan's six native dog breeds — which breed?
Shiba Inu: Japanese dog breed. The Shiba Inu (Japanese: 柴犬; Japanese pronunciation: [ɕi.ba.i.nɯ]) is a breed of hunting dog from Japan.

Originating in South America and rapidly diversifying after the extinction of the dinosaurs, this plant family — commonly known as the nightshades — includes toxic alkaloid-rich species alongside tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers. What family is it?
Built from four fused carbon rings, this class of organic compounds includes cholesterol, testosterone, and anabolic performance-enhancers — what is it called?
Steroid: Polycyclic organic compound having sterane as a core structure.
Native to the Balkan Peninsula, this fragrant flowering shrub in the olive family is cultivated widely across Europe and North America for its clusters of purple or white blooms — which species?
Syringa vulgaris: Plant species in the olive family.

This rare chromosomal condition gives affected females four copies of a single chromosome instead of the usual two, and is linked to distinctive facial features and skeletal quirks like incurved pinky fingers — what is it called?
Tetrasomy X: Chromosomal disorder with 4 X chromosomes.
Since joining Bethesda Game Studios in 1994, this director has overseen the Elder Scrolls and Fallout franchises as well as 2023's Starfield — who is he?
